Chapter 8: God’s Joy in Prayer and Communion.
You know those late-night talks where you really open up with a friend? Or maybe the feeling of writing a letter straight from the heart, or just sitting together in total trust and quiet. In moments like these, you feel a closeness—like all the barriers have faded away, and you’re really connecting. That’s the kind of closeness God finds joy in when we pray and spend time with Him.
A lot of folks see prayer as a chore, something to tick off a list, or maybe just a rescue rope when things go wrong. But there’s a bigger story here—one that’s all about relationship. It isn’t about checking the right boxes or saying the right words. It’s about being known, being heard. God isn’t far-off or uninterested. He actually delights in hearing us—our questions, our hopes, even our fears.
Picture this: someone sitting alone, not quite sure what to say, but choosing to speak anyway. Maybe the words come out awkward or broken. Maybe there’s just silence, or a sigh that says more than words ever could. That’s precious to God. He doesn’t care about fancy speeches—He listens for honesty. He welcomes our stammering, our pauses, our deepest sighs.
What really stands out is that prayer isn’t about getting everything perfect. It’s about drawing near, sharing life with God. You bring your joys, your disappointments, your dreams, your heartaches. And in those honest moments, something changes. The weight you’re carrying feels lighter. The loneliness eases. Hope starts to feel possible again.
Sometimes, it’s easy to slip into thinking God is too busy or too distant to care about what’s on your mind. But the truth is so much more tender than that. God’s heart is actually moved by our prayers. He delights in our trust, in those moments when we choose to come close. Prayer isn’t some transaction or business deal. It’s a relationship.
And when you start to see prayer that way, everything changes. It’s no longer about performing, or using the right words, or turning to God only when things fall apart. It becomes a way of living—a steady rhythm of conversation, a daily habit of drawing near.
Worship isn’t limited to a building or a set time. It’s the ongoing, everyday sharing of life with the One who always listens and delights in you.
